# Why 68% of Software Projects Fail

The Standish Group's CHAOS report consistently shows that **68% of software
projects fail or are challenged**. Not because teams lack talent — but because
the process breaks down.

## The three most common failure modes:

### 1. Requirements Drift

Business requirements are captured once, then slowly diverge from what gets
built. By the time you notice, months of work need to be redone.

**How the platform prevents it:** A dedicated Business Analyst agent produces
structured requirements with explicit acceptance criteria. The Critic agent
validates consistency at phase boundaries — drift is caught before code is
written.

### 2. Architecture-UX Disconnect

The architecture team designs one thing; the UX team designs another.
Integration reveals fundamental misalignments late in the cycle.

**How the platform prevents it:** All four disciplines (Business, Tech, UX,
Marketing) work from a shared Synthesis Report with a Cross-Team Blocker Matrix.
Dependencies are surfaced before implementation begins.

### 3. Security & Compliance Afterthoughts

Security reviews happen at the end — when the cost of change is highest.
Accessibility is tested just before launch. Compliance gaps delay shipping.

**How the platform prevents it:** Security Architect, Accessibility Specialist,
and Legal Counsel agents participate in the design phase. CI/CD includes
Gitleaks secret scanning, Trivy container scanning, and an automated
accessibility gate (WCAG 2.1 AA).
